propositions: Dual vocabulary ('Success Criteria' and 'Acceptance Criteria') in reviewer prompts and routing index creates spurious distinction and noise in rubrics, causing models to conflate unrelated criteria.
Renaming 'Success Criteria' to 'Acceptance Criteria' consistently across 10 prompt files and the routing index consolidates vocabulary at the source for all downstream generated artifacts.

The criteria routing edit rotates the registry version stamp, invalidating outstanding plan-review attestations as stale; this is safe only after ticket 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e (ADR 0053, which grandfathers drift) merges.

Three sites must be deliberately excluded from renaming: plan_review_T2.md (generic English for trial metrics), and dod_uncertifiable wording in both verifier prompts (separate concept, out of scope).
Regenerating the criteria guide from the renamed source is required and must retain the GENERATED banner; exactly one 'success criteria' match should survive (T2's embedded prompt).
Registry version rotation test must capture both pre-edit and post-edit stamps at runtime to prove the edit rotated the version without hard-coding literal values.
